cons: Automation continues running when context changes
Sub-processor chain for the model step needs tracking

name: Zapier AI
pros: No-code AI automation accessible to non-developers
Existing Zapier workflows gain AI steps without rebuilding
files: Handles the data formats and payloads of the connected apps.
value: Adds text-driven automation and AI actions to the workflows most organizations already run in Zapier. The value is the integration surface, 7,000-plus apps, not any particular model capability.
engine: Routes to third-party models (primarily OpenAI) through Zapier's action layer.
latency: Async by nature, suited to background automation rather than interactive use.

pricing.model: Per-task pricing within existing Zapier pricing

quality: Quality of the AI step depends on the underlying model. Value is in the connectivity, not the model.
tagline: AI layered on top of Zapier's automation network: 7,000 apps, text inputs, no code.
use_cases: Building AI-powered automations across SaaS tools without code
Routing, classifying, and acting on incoming data through natural language steps
Connecting AI outputs to downstream systems without building custom integrations
governance_note: Automation tools have a specific failure mode: they keep running when the world changes. An AI automation approved in one context will continue executing months later when the data, the counterparties, or the policy have shifted. Human review checkpoints must be designed in from the start, not added when something goes wrong. The audit question is not whether the automation worked today but whether anyone would know if it stopped working correctly.
training_optout: Follows OpenAI and any other sub-processor's terms for the model step. Zapier itself operates under its own data terms. Both matter.
